title: `calc(1 + 1px)` is kept as a valid length, and `sign(1em)` is folded to 1 at build time

regression.note: only for the derived 'drops a valid fallback' symptom (width:100px;width:calc(100% - 20)); the missing type check itself is older than 1.20

impact: Reporter's examples are agent-style (0 reactions, no project). But the type-check half covers a plausible real typo: a missing unit in calc, e.g. `calc(100% - 20)` or `calc(50% - 10)`. Browsers drop that declaration; Lightning CSS treats it as valid, so `.a{width:100px;width:calc(100% - 20)}` loses the valid 100px fallback, and `margin:0 auto;margin-left:calc(50% - 10)` becomes `margin:0 auto 0 calc(50% - 10)`, which the browser drops entirely (centering lost). Also no error in strict mode, so developers aren't told about the typo. The sign(1em) half only differs at font-size 0 (or a 0 viewport for vw) and is low.
code: src/values/calc.rs: Calc::add (number + value -> Calc::Sum with no type check), Calc::parse_sum
src/values/calc.rs: Calc::parse_with, "sign" arm (folds any try_map-able value, including em/rem/vw)

subcases.case: number + dimension accepted (calc(1 + 1px), calc(100% - 20), calc(1deg + 1), calc(1s + 1), calc(sign(1em) + 1px), hsl(from red calc(h + 1deg) s l))
subcases.cause: Calc trees don't track a calc type; Calc::add pairs Calc::Number with Value/Sum/Function freely. For relative colors, h is a <number> channel so h + 1deg is invalid (Chromium rejects it) but is folded into a valid color #ff0400
subcases.fix: medium: add a type check at +/- in parse_sum (a small 'calc kind' function: Number vs dimension, products take their non-number side, sign() is Number, min/max/clamp/abs/round take their args' kind) and return InvalidValue on mismatch. Watch relative-color channel keywords and Calc<CSSNumber> contexts.

subcases.cause: sign arm folds whenever v.try_map succeeds; only percentages are excluded
subcases.status: confirmed, low (fringe: differs only when the reference size is 0)
subcases.fix: small: only fold when the value is absolute (to_px() is Some) or the numeric value is 0; otherwise keep MathFunction::Sign

summary: Calc::add never type-checks a + or - sub-expression, so `calc(<number> + <length>)` parses as a length. css-values-4 Type Checking makes the whole calculation invalid, and Chromium drops it. Because the declaration is typed as valid, deduplication and shorthand merging then let it replace valid declarations, which changes rendering (browser-verified). Separately, sign() of a font/viewport-relative length is folded to 1 at build time, wrong only when that length resolves to 0.
repro: 1402-repro.mjs. `.a{width:calc(1 + 1px)}` -> kept, no error/warning. `.a{width:100px;width:calc(100% - 20)}` -> `.a{width:calc(100% - 20)}`. `.a{margin:0 auto;margin-left:calc(50% - 10)}` -> `.a{margin:0 auto 0 calc(50% - 10)}`. `hsl(from red calc(h + 1deg) s l)` -> `#ff0400`. `calc(sign(1em) * 10px)` -> `10px`; `calc(5px + 10px * sign(1em))` -> `15px`. Controls: `calc(sign(2px) * 10px)` -> 10px, `sign(100vw - 600px)` kept, `calc(1px + 1em)` kept, `hsl(from red calc(h + 1) s l)` kept, `line-height:calc(1 + 0.5)` -> 1.5.

If this returns failure, the entire calculation's type is failure.' sign(): 'returns ... 0⁺ if A's numeric value is 0⁺'.

fix.approach: Type-check +/- in Calc::parse_sum (calc.rs) so mismatched sums fail to parse; the property then falls back to an error in strict mode / a preserved unparsed declaration with a warning in errorRecovery, which no longer participates in dedupe/merging. Separately restrict the sign() fold to absolute lengths. Add tests in src/lib.rs next to the calc tests; check existing expectations that contain number+dimension sums.

draftReply:
Thanks, both confirmed on master and 1.31-1.33.

`calc()` sums aren't type-checked, so `calc(1 + 1px)` is treated as a valid length. Beyond the missing error, this matters for a common typo like a forgotten unit: `.a{width:100px;width:calc(100% - 20)}` minifies to just the invalid declaration, so the browser loses the `100px` fallback, and `margin:0 auto;margin-left:calc(50% - 10)` merges into a `margin` shorthand the browser drops. Per [CSS Values 4 type checking](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-4/#calc-type-checking) the sum is invalid, and Chromium rejects it.

The `sign(1em)` fold is also wrong in principle (it's 0 at `font-size: 0`), though that only matters in that edge case.
